mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 5.25% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.25% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and causes S&P 500 to underperform over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of quarters where GDPC1 falls below -2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 4.0% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.0% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in INDPRO and a fall in HOUST above 5% over two months indicates supply chain normalization with reduced housing demand pressure, which boosts corporate margins and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > +5% and HOUST < -5% over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly above zero in more than 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in RSAFS above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% signals rising household savings and reduced consumption, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where RSAFS exceeds its 12-month MA by more than 10%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above 5% for two months signals a dual shock of higher rates and inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL > 5% for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of such dual-shock episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly increase in PAYEMS above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly above zero in more than 60% of such labor expansion episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on negative relationship exists between HOUST and S&P 500 5-day returns: higher housing starts are associated with stronger near-term economic activity and positive equity returns within the next week.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly above zero when HOUST rises month-over-month in more than 70% of cases.
